nodes.text: Shade's free, windfalls aren't — the cows have taught me to say that up front. What brings you under my trees?

choices.text: What's this war with the cows?

nodes.text: My Hollis planted the old oak at the east end the year we married — said a wedding wants a witness that'll outlive the gossip. I planted the rest around him when he passed, so he'd have company and I'd have somewhere to put my talking. Forty trees now. He always was a good listener; being an orchard's only improved him.

The pasture cows have declared my windfalls a public entitlement. I've been to the moot *twice*. Motion carried, fence approved — and the next morning that brindled matriarch had the gate latch open like she'd read the minutes. I respect her. I'm going to lose this war to her. But there'll be a record, and history will know I fought.
Here — berry pressings and a slice of feast cake, because anybody polite enough to ask under the trees gets fed under them. {item:cake} Hollis's rule. The orchard enforces it now.
Mind where you step — windfalls underfoot, and every one of them legally contested.
